statement: A fresh CREATE whose replica has been admitted into its partition's committed configuration never turns an unavailable authority read into an orphaned configured member. The create-admission authorization of releaseFreshCreate answers a typed UNAVAILABLE{create_admission_authority, retryAfterMs, cause} that the existing participant-release completion operation consumes within the create's existing deadline, so a transient refusal of the replica_operations read (as at 10:29:57 on run b26d2c090) delays the create instead of failing it. When the create does fail after admission committed, its FAILED transition always carries the failed-create cleanup claim, so the existing failed-create cleanup owner removes the member through a committed REMOVE; the cleanup decision is made from the committed admission fact, never from error.deferRetry, and a FAILED row from a create in flight is protected from the planner's FAILED cure only while a claim or a live create owner exists. The one-shot authorization throw, the deferRetry-based claimCleanup arm and the unconditional previous_state protection are deleted.

constraints.statement: Instance of the class 'a typed unavailability is converted into a terminal failure that abandons a committed obligation' (authority-and-recovery.md 'A refusal has an owned consequence', :138-145; regression-policy Structured Deferred-Outcome). The repair is made at the create-admission/create-failure owners for every fresh CREATE, not for sql_transactions-p1 or priority partitions only.

Reuses participant-release-client.js completeParticipantRelease (quest participant-release-completion-owner, landed at 132ff5185, awaiting certification) unchanged: same trigger, authorization identity, measured build, caller clock and absolute deadline; no budget renewal. Authorization is re-read from the authority on each attempt; a refused or stale row is never authorization; the cached replica_operations row is never consulted.

The readiness-projection routing refusal that caused the 10:29:57 read failure (census C5, readiness-observation-currency.md) is not repaired or excepted here: no routing carve-out, fail-open or priority bypass. This quest makes the create survive any authority unavailability, whatever its cause.

fenceFailedReplicaCreateRuntime and replica-cleanup-host-custody semantics are consumed unchanged; the target never proposes a configuration change itself and no synthetic REMOVE event is introduced. Removal flows through the existing failed-create cleanup claim and owner.

Red first at the production entry path (createReplicaAsync through voter-ready with an authority read answering {success:false} then normally; deadline spent; restart after FAILED without claim), then one live witness of fresh-formation-user-table-routability on local-three-node.json showing no FAILED configured member without a cleanup claim and no create failing on a single deferred read. Scenario green is not claimed (C1/C10 and C5 remain).

The first divergence is recorded in evidence/first-divergence-2026-11-02.md (run b26d2c090, 10:29:57.228). A new witness that moves the first divergence elsewhere is recorded before any further src/ change; a repair is not called complete because a different later step fails.

No timeout, deadline or budget increase; no new timer, retry loop, alias, fallback, carve-out, cache wait, synthetic event, '|| default' that turns a missing input into success, or cache/SQL dual path. Rejected remedies listed in evidence/design-note.md (section Deletions) are not reintroduced without new evidence and an explicit owner decision.

Live runs only through node scripts/lab.js (fleet first, dry-run first, one scenario run at a time, thermal admission, no cluster node on the controller, no pruning on lab hosts). Raw logs are kept outside the repository in lagrange-evidence-store/<run-id>/; quest evidence holds summaries and sha256 digests.
If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.
